extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent applicants and practitioners involved in interference/derivation proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for suggesting, searching for, preparing, and managing interferences/derivation proceedings (including applicant suggestions, examiner actions, written‑description and priority showings, claim sorting, and related procedural requirements) under pre‑AIA rules and 37 CFR subpart provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applications and adding non-corresponding claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board does not permit reissue applicants to add claims that would not correspond to a count (Winter v. Fujita).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue applications are not subject to patent term adjustments; burden lies with the reissue applicant to comply with Winter, so an examiner need not require restriction of non-interfering claims. Practice under Winter may explain multiple reissue filings by an applicant who seeks to amend claims in response to an interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature interference requests when examination not complete
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for interference is premature if examination of the application has not been completed as required by 37 CFR 41.102(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 23.01 may be used to acknowledge a premature request. Consideration of a potential interference should be deferred until examination is complete. See MPEP § 2303.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary suspensions; issue allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspensions should rarely, if ever, be used and applications with allowed claims should be issued to the greatest extent possible (because applicants may be eligible for patent term adjustments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) An interference may not be declared between two patents — do not hold an allowable claim to issue simply to await interference. (2) If one application is complete and the other is not, the complete application should generally issue; suspensions must not be used to create ties between applications. If issuance as patent creates prior art, appropriate rejections should be made or a priority showing required (37 CFR 41.202(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to suggest interference based on earliest effective filing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If two applications are both ready to issue, an interference may be suggested if their earliest effective filing dates are within six months of each other; if more than six months apart, the earlier-filed application should issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application E's earliest effective filing date is more than six months before F's, E should issue. If issuance would make E prior art against F, make the appropriate rejection; if not, require a priority showing (37 CFR 41.202(d) and MPEP § 2305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve outstanding patent issues before suggesting interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents that are subject to other outstanding USPTO proceedings (reexamination, reissue, late maintenance fee petitions, disclaimers, corrections, inventorship corrections, etc.) ordinarily must have those issues resolved before an interference is suggested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) If maintenance fee not timely paid and patent considered expired, an interference cannot be declared unless a petition to accept delayed payment is granted. (2) A statutory disclaimer or correction that removes the sole claim directed to the same invention eliminates the basis for interference. (3) Inventorship correction that makes inventors the same eliminates basis for interference under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may suggest an interference and examiner consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: A suggestion for an interference may come from an applicant or an examiner; whoever suggests it determines what must be shown prior to declaration, and the examiner must consult with an Interference Practice Specialist (IPS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPS may refer suggested interferences to the Board; examine the relevant requirements depending on whether suggestion is by applicant or examiner and consult the IPS when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference search requirement when application in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is in condition for allowance, an interference search must be made using the most efficient and effective means based on the claimed subject matter in the broadest claim (text search, classified search, or combination, of US-PGPUB database).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider each effective filing date (continuation-in-part issues) when searching. If claims involve nucleotide/amino acid sequences, request STIC to perform sequence interference search. Make the search of record (MPEP § 719.05 III). Search must be extended to all classes/subgroups necessary (not limited to classification of the application). Include applications under Secrecy Order when required; request inspection of paper files/prints/drawings via Licensing and Review when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and control involved files; assignment to same examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications believed to interfere should ordinarily be assigned to the same examiner; complete patent and benefit files (IFW or paper) must be available before referring a suggested interference to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper file wrapper is lost it must be reconstructed. PCT application files are generally not separate unless benefit is claimed to the PCT itself. Reassignment may be necessary when involved applications are in different Technology Centers; ordinarily reassign to the TC where the commonly claimed invention would be classified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified translation requirement for non-English benefit documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified translation of every foreign benefit application or PCT application not filed in English is required for the benefit to be accorded (35 U.S.C. 119(b)(3), 372(b)(3); 37 CFR 1.55(g)(3)(i), 41.154(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no certified translation is in the official record, the examiner must require one. Any showing of priority relying on a non-English application is prima facie insufficient without a certified English translation. Use Form paragraph 23.19 to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sorting and consolidating claims to mitigate interference delay
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant has related applications with interfering claims intermixed with non-interfering claims, the examiner should consider consolidating interfering claims into a single application or requiring restriction of an application to non-interfering claims so examination can proceed for non-interfering claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interfering claims of applications with same assignee or inventive entity are 'patentably indistinct claims' under 37 CFR 1.78(f); the examiner may require consolidation into a single application that provides support. Alternatively require restriction in accordance with pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 121 and permit a divisional for non-interfering claims. Do not consolidate a claim into an application that lacks 35 U.S.C. 112(a) support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant suggestion formal requirements (37 CFR 41.202(a) checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant suggests an interference, the suggestion must: (1) provide sufficient information to identify the other application/patent; (2) identify all claims the applicant believes interfere, propose one or more counts, and show claim-to-count correspondence; (3) for each count provide a claim chart comparing at least one claim of each party and show why they interfere under § 41.203(a); (4) explain in detail why applicant will prevail on priority; (5) if a claim was added/amended to provoke an interference provide a claim chart showing written description for each claim in the applicant’s specification; (6) for each constructive reduction to practice for which benefit is requested provide a chart showing where the disclosure provides that constructive reduction-to-practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 23.06–23.06.06 may be used to acknowledge or indicate specific formal deficiencies. Examiner reviews for formal sufficiency but is generally not responsible for substantive adequacy of priority showings, though may offer observations to accompany referral to the Board (Form PTO-850).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for applicant to correct deficiencies when suggesting interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is given TWO (2) MONTHS from the mailing date of the deficiency communication to correct deficiencies; extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but reply cannot be extended beyond statutory maximum of SIX MONTHS (35 U.S.C. 133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 23.06.06 to set the reply period; include bracketed dates as required by the form paragraph instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the other application or patent (practical guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing the serial number or patent number will fully meet the identification requirement; if applicant relies on indirect evidence (journal, patent pending notice, foreign publication), names of likely inventors/assignees may assist identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should help the examiner identify the other application because inadequate information may prevent declaration of the suggested interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counts and requirement to identify patentable claims for each count
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must identify at least one patentable claim from every application or patent that interferes for each proposed count; a count describes the interfering subject matter used by the Board to determine admissible priority evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must confirm that (A) at least one patentable count is identified, (B) at least one patentable claim from each party is identified for each count, and (C) a claim chart comparing at least one set of claims for each count is provided. Examiner need not agree with applicant’s substantive position—role is to confirm interfering claims and formalities of 37 CFR 41.202 are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explaining and proving priority when applicant's earliest constructive reduction is later
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant's earliest constructive reduction-to-practice is later than the apparent earliest for the other party, the applicant must show why it would prevail on priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may (A) antedate the other party's constructive reduction, (B) demonstrate why the other party is not entitled to its apparent earliest constructive reduction, or (C) provide other reasons why applicant should be considered prior inventor. The showing may resemble 37 CFR 1.130–1.132 showings but differs in scope; examiner generally does not examine substantive adequacy except certain situations (e.g., overcoming 102(a)/(e) rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner role when suggestion attempts to overcome a 102(a) or 102(e) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant suggests an interference instead of filing a declaration under 37 CFR 1.130–1.132 to overcome a 102(a) or 102(e) rejection, the examiner must review the suggestion to verify that the applicant's showing, taken at face value, is sufficient to overcome the rejection; if not sufficient, examination is not completed and the suggestion should not be referred to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must maintain the rejection and not refer the suggestion if the showing is inadequate to overcome the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 135(b) (one‑year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim was added or an application filed more than one year after issuance/publication of the potentially interfering patent/application, an interference will not be declared unless at least one claim present prior to the one‑year cutoff is for 'substantially the same subject matter' as a claim of the patent/published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination uses a 'substantially the same' test based on presence/absence of different material limitations (not an obviousness test). If none of the pre‑cutoff claims meet the test, the interfering claim should be rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 135(b). Form paragraphs 23.14 and 23.14.01 may be used for rejections under 135(b)(1) and 135(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate written description requirement for interfering claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is not entitled to an interference merely because the applicant requests one—the interfering claim must be allowable with respect to written description under 35 U.S.C. 112(a); written description is satisfied if the application/priority application sufficiently describes the subject matter to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written description does not necessarily require examples or an actual reduction-to-practice. Added or amended claims to provoke an interference receive heightened scrutiny; copied claims are construed in view of the originating specification when challenged. Written description unavailability can be a threshold issue in an interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide written-description claim chart for added/amended provocation claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim has been added or amended to provoke an interference, applicant must provide a claim chart showing the written description for each claim in the applicant's specification (37 CFR 41.202(a)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 23.06.05 addresses failure to provide such a chart. Failure to show written description support is a formal deficiency and a substantive threshold for entitlement to interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee limitations on suggesting interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee cannot suggest an interference under 37 CFR 41.202 but may, to the extent permitted under 37 CFR 1.291, alert the examiner of an application claiming interfering subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patentee may only suggest via becoming an applicant (e.g., by filing a reissue application) or by alerting the examiner under limited rules; see MPEP §§ 1134 and 1901 for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require adding a claim to provoke interference (conditions and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may require an applicant to add a claim to provoke an interference; failure to satisfy the requirement within the set period will operate as a concession of priority for that subject matter. For interference with a patent, the applicant must also comply with paragraphs (a)(2)–(a)(6) of 37 CFR 41.202.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim required by the examiner must: (1) be patentable to the applicant, and (2) be drawn to patentable subject matter claimed by another applicant/patentee. Before requiring such a claim, the examiner should consult with an IPS and follow guiding principles (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles for examiner discretion in requiring a claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles to guide whether an examiner should require an interfering claim: (A) generally do not suggest interference if examination is not otherwise completed; (B) the required claim must not encompass prior art or otherwise be barred; (C) the application must provide adequate support under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for the required claim; (D) do not require a claim when applicant expressly states the commonly described subject matter is not the applicant’s invention; (E) a claim based on a claim from a published application should not be required unless that published claim has been allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given cost and complexity of interferences, the requirement should not be lightly made; consult with IPS before making the requirement. Examples illustrate when a requirement is inappropriate (e.g., patent is prior art, time-bar issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: When an interfering claim already exists in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant already has a claim to the same subject matter as a claim in another application/patent, there is no need to require adding a claim to have a basis for an interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may invite the applicant to suggest an interference pursuant to 37 CFR 41.202(a). If applicant does not suggest one, the examiner should work with an IPS to suggest an interference to the Board and include an explanation of why at least one claim of each application/patent defines the same invention (complete Form PTO-850).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner preparation for discussion with IPS/Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should be prepared to discuss: why claims interfere, whether the subject matter of other claims would have been anticipated or rendered obvious if interfering claims are treated as prior art, and whether a party is entitled to constructive reduction-to-practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPS may require the examiner to prepare a memorandum for the Board or participate in a conference to discuss the suggested interference. Be ready to explain interfering claim relationships and entitlement to benefit claims.
